answers.answer: Rule is the player with more warriors plus buildings than every other player in the clearing. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Tokens and pawns do not count, and Vagabond cannot rule or prevent rule.

A normal move takes a positive number of your warriors or pawns along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and you must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move, and the same pieces may move repeatedly, including within one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.

The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits, uncapped by defending warriors, and the battle ends if the attacker has no warriors or pawns left. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die is attacker's hits, lower is defender's; Alliance reverses dice), then after-roll effects. Rolled hits are capped by each side's warriors in battle, except Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead. Add extra hits and subtract ignored hits; a defender with no warriors is defenseless for one extra attacker hit, while Vagabond is defenseless with no undamaged swords. Each hit removes one opposing piece; the hit side chooses removal order but removes all warriors before buildings/tokens, and chooses order of removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal counted hits. Removing an enemy building/token scores its remover 1 VP each, including a defender; Vagabond instead takes item damage.

Craft from hand by activating your faction's crafting pieces matching the card's bottom-left crafting icons, not by paying its suit. A crafting piece activates only once per turn, except Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from map supply. A persistent effect already in your play area cannot be crafted again; persistent cards stay there and are not available to spend as hand cards.

During your Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance requires ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced. Dominance cards cannot be crafted, but can be spent for suit.

When a dominance card is spent, put it near the map as available instead of in the discard pile. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand; available bird dominance remains bird and requires a bird payment, while a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance card. Taking a card does not activate it; activation is a separate Daylight choice.

With two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins; the map supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. Keep the four R-marked ruin items separate; only Vagabond setup hides one bag, boot, hammer and sword, one under each ruin. With no Vagabond, ruins have no items. Setup factions in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond order; this does not determine turn order.

Only Marquise may place pieces in the keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed. Whenever Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors at the keep instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Without a keep, there is no Field Hospitals destination.

Marquise Daylight crafts with workshops first, then takes up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order. Battle is one battle; March is up to two moves as one compound action; Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn; Build uses the wood network and a clearing Marquise rules; Overwork spends a matching card to place one wood at a sawmill. The supplied summary gives no separate numerical limit for Recruit beyond once per turn, and no additional action limit beyond those stated.

Build in a clearing you rule with an open slot, selecting a building type and taking its leftmost building. Pay the column cost in wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the uncovered track space; full cost, a building and a legal slot are required.

Eyrie Birdsong: draw one card if hand is empty; add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns, at most one of them a bird; then, if no roosts are on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Eyrie crafts with roosts, then resolves every Decree column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Within a column it chooses card order freely; birds are wild. Recruit requires a roost in a clearing matching the card suit; Move starts in a matching clearing and follows ordinary move rules; Battle occurs in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no existing roost. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil starts immediately and later cards/columns are not skipped to.

In Turmoil, lose 1 VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up; then retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and play proceeds to Evening. Map warriors and buildings remain. Eyrie still scores its roost track in Evening, even after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie > Turmoil; Evening, even after turmoil.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing; that player adds one matching hand card, with birds matching any suit, to Supporters. A group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If no matching card including birds is held, show the hand to Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. The supporter capacity still applies.

In Birdsong, Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt targets a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on its board, costs two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces, scores 1 VP per enemy building/token removed, places the matching base, warriors equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings, and one officer; enemy Vagabond instead damages three items. Spread Sympathy targets an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy (or any clearing if none exists), pays the supporter cost shown above its next token, plus one matching supporter if one other player has at least three warriors there (Martial Law), then places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. Only one sympathy per clearing.

Train in Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay Train. In Evening, each officer permits one operation, including Organize: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there and score the uncovered VP. Losing a base discards all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, removes half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain reduces supporters to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance > Losing a base; Daylight; Evening.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step adds no refresh then. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, including into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination has any hostile faction's warriors; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items; the Vagabond then always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, discards to five, and checks capacity.

Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a track, and scores 1 VP if an item is taken; removing the ruin's last item frees its building slot. Quest exhausts its two listed items, completes the quest, and chooses VP equal to completed matching quests including this one or draws two cards; a replacement quest is revealed. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction makes that faction Hostile immediately, except the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. On the Vagabond's own turn, battle removal of hostile pieces scores 1 extra VP per hostile piece, except the warrior that first made the faction Hostile; ordinary building/token VP is also scored. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though it may still acquire a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove a warrior, or another faction piece only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Relationships: Hostile, Infamy; Aid; Strike.

answers.answer: With four or more players, Vagabond may in its Daylight at 10 or more VP activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in one, choosing among players with the lowest VP other than Vagabond. It places its score marker on that faction board and stops scoring; if the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. The supplied summary does not state an additional eligibility restriction for the partner beyond not already being in a coalition. Coalition partners are not enemies; a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent, and coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers.

Cards override the Law, and the Law overrides Learning to Play. Follow general and faction rules together when possible; where incompatible, the faction rule wins. A “cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden.

If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

At-start effects happen before all other effects of the phase; at-end effects happen after them but before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public but contents are private; reveal or show cards only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected, but the deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.

When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including forced non-bird give/discard instructions and multiple same-suit payments; a non-bird cannot substitute when bird is explicitly required.

Pieces are finite and cannot be proxied. If instructed to place, take or remove more pieces than are available, do as many as possible; shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not excuse Eyrie from completing Decree actions. For Marquise Recruit shortage, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters.
answers.evidence: Actions > Battle, removed pieces; Marquise > Recruit.

answers.answer: Pieces placed normally come from supply (or the leftmost track space); pieces removed normally return to supply (or the rightmost empty track space). Items removed from the game are permanently removed. When removals are simultaneous, remove all the pieces before triggering removal effects.
Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes that battle's decisions.

An enemy cannot place a piece in the Keep clearing, including by replacing a piece, because replacement requires both removal and a legal placement. Other players may move pieces into that clearing. A swap ignores move/place restrictions; it is not treated as a move or a place.
If several players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

Forest adjacency follows the map: forests are adjacent if separated by just one printed path; a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path. Winter's river also divides forests, affecting adjacency for Slip. Fall has no special rules.
answers.evidence: Actions > Shared movement; setup map rules.

answers.answer: Marquise starts with 25 warriors and 8 wood in supply. Put the Keep in any corner and one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any slot-legal combination. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

Eyrie takes 20 warriors, then places one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed for that leader; keep the other leaders face up nearby. Put the other six roosts on the track from right to left.

Alliance has 10 warriors in supply, three bases in their matching board spaces, and ten sympathy on its track. It draws three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from its three-card hand. It starts with no map pieces and no officers.

Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest; shuffle quests and display three face up. Take character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel, and return unused S items to the box. Set each other faction's relationship marker to Indifferent.

Recommended total Reach is at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5 and Alliance 3. The summary also says the Law permits adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

In Birdsong, Marquise places one wood at each sawmill, limited by its eight-wood supply; multiple sawmills in one clearing each produce one. In Evening, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard down to five.
Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, but only once per turn. If supply cannot fill every recruiter, place the maximum available; Marquise chooses among eligible recruiters.
Eyrie crafts items using roosts. Its Disdain for Trade makes crafted items score 1 VP instead of their printed VP; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.
answers.evidence: Eyrie > Lords of the Forest / Disdain for Trade.

answers.answer: Builder: Recruit and Move Viziers; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; gets one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; removing at least one enemy building/token in battle scores one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.
No. The Decree must be fully completed; with Charismatic, each Recruit must place two warriors. A single remaining warrior cannot fulfill that Recruit, so Eyrie enters Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Decree Recruit; Turmoil on any incomplete action.

answers.answer: Guerrilla War does not bypass warrior limits: rolled hits remain capped by each side's warriors in battle. When Alliance defends, Alliance uses the higher die and the attacker the lower.
No: Supporters cannot be used for crafting. Alliance can inspect its face-down Supporter stack, and Supporters do not count as hand cards or toward its hand limit of five.
No. In Birdsong, Revolt happens before Spread Sympathy, so sympathy newly placed later in that Birdsong cannot be revolted during the earlier Revolt step.

No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors of one other player in the chosen clearing; two warriors from each of two players do not qualify. Martial Law is a Spread Sympathy supporter surcharge; Organize has no Martial Law cost.

Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it either. If Vagabond moves Allied faction warriors into sympathy, that warrior movement does trigger Outrage for the player moving them.
answers.evidence: Alliance > Outrage; Vagabond > Move with ally.

answers.answer: In Evening, Alliance may take Move, Battle, Recruit or Organize operations in any order and number up to its officer count. Using an officer does not remove it; officers stay on the board. After operations, draw one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discard to five.
The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead damage three Vagabond items.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Pawn and items; Alliance Revolt.

answers.answer: Vagabond's rolled-hit cap is the number of all its undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or face down. It is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. If taking hits, each hit damages one undamaged item of its choice; excess hits are ignored once no undamaged items remain. The summary says damage leaves the item's face unchanged.
answers.evidence: Battle > Roll/Count hits; Vagabond > Pawn and items.

answers.answer: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty space on their matching track if possible; each track holds at most three. Exhausting an item on track sends it to Satchel. Ready tea/coins/bags repaired or returned from damage move onto tracks when there is space. Damaged items cannot pay for actions.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Pawn and items; Repair; Evening Rest.

answers.answer: Capacity is six items plus two for each face-up bag on its track. Count items in both Satchel and Damaged box; track items do not count. Check at the final Evening capacity step, not immediately on acquiring an item, and permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within the limit.

No. Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Birdsong Refresh flips exhausted items face up; Repair moves one damaged item to Satchel while keeping its current face.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest.

answers.answer: Aid costs exhausting any one item and giving the player with faction pieces in the clearing a card matching the clearing (birds count); no crafted item is required to perform Aid. Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items box, if available. To improve a non-Hostile relationship by one space requires as many Aids to that faction in the same turn as the number printed between the spaces; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. At Allied status, each subsequent Aid scores 2 VP.

At Allied status, subsequent Aid scores 2 VP each. Vagabond may move warriors of one Allied faction with it, subject to their own movement restrictions and Eyrie tie advantage; they cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. In battle, it may use warriors of one Allied faction as its own against another enemy, but cannot use them to attack that ally itself.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Relationships: Move with ally; Attack with ally.

answers.answer: At battle end, the ally becomes Hostile if Vagabond removed more of its allied warriors as hits than the number of Vagabond items it damaged in that battle. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those allied warriors removed as hits; equal counts do not trigger it.

No. Vagabond crafting requires the current clearing to match all crafting icons, so a single clearing cannot satisfy mixed fox and rabbit requirements. The pawn may activate repeatedly by exhausting a hammer for each crafting icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel or a matching track.

Thief starts with boot, torch, tea and sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag and hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow and sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items, keeping their faces, then immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.
Taking a ruin's last hidden item removes the ruin and frees the building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not remove one.
Coalition partners are not enemies, so a coalition partner cannot be attacked as an enemy. Coalition does not automatically grant Allied relationship powers.

The Vagabond scores 2 VP for removing the two warriors as hostile pieces, plus 1 VP for removing the building, for 3 VP total. The first warrior that made that faction Hostile does not earn Infamy, while the second does; the building earns the ordinary removal VP.

A normal Vagabond move exhausts one boot. It costs one extra boot if the destination contains any warriors of any Hostile faction; hostile buildings alone do not add a boot, and hostile warriors from multiple factions still trigger only the one extra boot.
Taking an available dominance card into hand does not activate it; activation is separate. Taking and activating dominance each occur during Daylight and neither requires a faction action allowance.

Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns the chosen faction and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces; possessing an item does not make it owned by the faction holding it.

An immediate-effect crafting card is resolved and discarded; a persistent-effect card remains in the play area. A persistent card there is outside the hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

Ambush and dominance cards cannot be crafted. Ambush cards may be played in battle as ambushes; dominance cards may be activated or spent for suit, and a spent dominance card becomes available near the map rather than going to discard.

Choose starting player and seating randomly. Put score markers at zero and set battle dice nearby; faction setup is in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond order. Setup order is distinct from turn order; turns proceed clockwise.
The first player to 30 VP wins immediately; they do not finish the action, phase or turn first.

To initiate an ordinary battle, choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy faction as defender. The summary does not state that you must rule the clearing; ordinary rule is not listed as a battle requirement.

For simultaneous battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses the order of both players' before-roll effects and of both players' after-roll effects. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by its own pieces being removed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Battle > Before-roll, After-roll and Deal hits.

answers.answer: In Count Hits, add extra hits and subtract hits ignored by effects.

When a non-Vagabond faction crafts an item, take it from the map item supply into its Crafted Items box and score the item's listed VP, except Eyrie usually scores only 1 VP due to Disdain for Trade. The summary does not specify a more precise physical supply location than map item supply.
answers.evidence: Actions > Craft; Eyrie > Disdain for Trade.

answers.answer: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy. A crafting piece's suit is its clearing's suit. A three-color question-mark crafting icon accepts any suit.

Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, respecting the supporter cap. Alliance may Craft, Mobilize and Train in any order and number during Daylight, so it need not finish all crafting before Mobilizing or Training.
In an ordinary Evening, Eyrie scores the VP shown on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draws one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discards down to five. It still scores after Turmoil.

Vagabond exhausts one sword to initiate its Daylight Battle action. An exhausted but undamaged sword still counts toward rolled hits, but cannot pay an action cost because paying requires exhausting a face-up undamaged item.
answers.evidence: Vagabond > Daylight Battle; Pawn and items.

answers.answer: Turn phases are Birdsong, Daylight, Evening; turns proceed clockwise, so after Evening the next clockwise player's Birdsong begins.

For each hit, Vagabond chooses one undamaged item to damage and moves it to the Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.
